dedupe_keys.name: spatially explicit inventory of phosphorus in sydney s organic wastes and agricultural demand 2011 100 m grid

description: This gridded inventory maps how much phosphorus, a fertiliser nutrient, is contained in the organic wastes produced across Greater Sydney and where farms in the region need it, as a basis for planning to recycle waste back to agriculture. The producers are Genevieve Metson of Linköping University, Dana Cordell and Steve Mohr of the University of Technology Sydney and Brad Ridoutt of the national science agency CSIRO. Coverage is the Greater Sydney Basin on a 100 metre grid for 2011, with scenarios for the future; the authors found fifteen times more phosphorus in organic waste than local agricultural demand, and tested a scenario with plant-based diets, no edible food waste and no local animal production. The zipped grid files and readme are available as a free download from Dryad, mirrored on Zenodo, under the CC0 dedication. Caveats: the waste streams and methods behind each layer are documented in the readme and article, values are modelled estimates for one year, and the archive is large. Simulation uses: siting organic waste processing and nutrient recovery facilities, optimising transport of recovered fertiliser to farms, and linking waste and food supply systems. Related records: the FAO food loss and waste database (data-fao-food-loss-and-waste-database) and What a Waste (data-what-a-waste-global-database) give broader waste statistics.
